read_surface_residual_attribution.case: hydra_to_native_read_surface (search io\nread(o1).write(o0) vs the displayed gradient surface o1)
read_surface_residual_attribution.observed: Fails only at 96x48 (144/18,432 bytes, max delta 1); exact at 64x64. All differing bytes are +1 and confined to the gradient coordinate channels: red of column x=81 (216->217) for all 48 rows and green of row y=41 (220->221) for all 96 columns.
read_surface_residual_attribution.controlled_probe: A probe page rendered gradient(speed: 0) to o1, then compared three read paths against the displayed o1 bytes at both sizes: (a) hydra src(tex: o1).write(o0) — 0 bytes differ at 64x64 AND 96x48 (the port's own surface-sampling path is exact); (b) engine io read(o1).write(o0), first render after compile — an all-black frame (12,288/12,288 differ at 64x64; 13,824/18,432 differ, max 255, at 96x48); (c) the same io read re-rendered — correct values with exactly the 96x48 signature (144 bytes, max 1) and exact at 64x64.
read_surface_residual_attribution.mechanism: The io read path carries an fp16 (half-float) precision step. Modeling each gradient coordinate value as fp16-round-tripped before 8-bit quantization predicts the observed failure set exactly: at 64x64 every value 255*(2n+1)/128 is exactly representable in fp16 (no rounding pixels — case exact); at 96x48 exactly two values are not: x=81 gives fp16(163/192)=0.849121 -> 217 (vs 216.484 -> 216) and y=41 gives fp16(83/96)=0.864746 -> 221 (vs 220.469 -> 220). Model prediction matches the observed pixels, channels, direction (+1), and values exactly.
read_surface_residual_attribution.ownership: The io namespace and its read starter are registered by the Noisemaker engine (loaded from the CDN), not by this port: the port registers only the hydra namespace (src/engine/portHydraEffects.js registers HYDRA_NAMESPACE='hydra' exclusively). The port's own surface-sampling path (hydra src(tex: o1)) is byte-exact at both sizes.
read_surface_residual_attribution.classification: Same automation-unsatisfiable class as the attributed rotate_animated_parameter residual on this host: an engine-internal precision artifact, not a port translation or engine-evaluation difference. It is documented, not tolerated: the case is unchanged, the strict zero-failure policy is unchanged, and closing it requires an exact-parity host or an explicitly ratified residual policy.

time_point_coverage.definition: The Hydra effect catalog exposes no seed inputs (grep of src/glsl/glsl-functions.js and src/glsl/utility-functions.js finds no seed input), so seed coverage reduces to time-point coverage for the time-dependent fixtures. Time-dependence is determined per fixture from the effect bodies: the noise generator's body is _noise(vec3(_st*scale, offset*time)), so any chain with noise offset != 0 is time-dependent — this covers parameter_matrix (noise offset 2.5) and parameter_matrix_combine (nested noise offset 0.2); osc is time-dependent through its time*sync term (sync 0.2 in the nonzero-time cases); voronoi is time-dependent through its time*speed term (speed 0.3); the gradient-speed-0, contrast/hue/saturate, shape/scroll(speeds 0)/posterize chains have no time-dependent inputs, so parameter_matrix_color and parameter_matrix_geometry render identical bytes at any time — their second time points are still included and executed explicitly rather than relying on inferred invariance.
time_point_coverage.executed: One additional time point per parameterized and time-dependent fixture, all as matched legacy-vs-port comparisons: osc_nonzero_time_t075 (t=0.75), voronoi_src_t075 (t=0.75), parameter_matrix_t075 (t=0.75), parameter_matrix_color_t05 (t=0.5), parameter_matrix_geometry_t06 (t=0.6), parameter_matrix_combine_t075 (t=0.75).
